brief:
A water-to-air charge cooler for the turbo kit on my 250 cc kart engine, printed in AlSi10Mg on a
metal powder-bed machine, built along +Z. All I have is the space: a 110 x 80 x 60 mm box (x along the
110, y across the 80, z up, origin at a bottom corner), and the cooler and its fittings must fit in it.
The boost air comes in through the x = 0 end and leaves through the x = 110 end; put the coolant
connections wherever suits. At full boost it's about 0.015 kg/s of air at 130 C off the compressor and I
want it out at 70 C or cooler. The coolant is 50/50 glycol, 3 L/min at 40 C. No more than 0.1 bar lost on
the air side (it eats boost), 0.2 bar on the coolant side, and keep it under 300 g.
